name: SSI2131
description: Analog-synth voltage-controlled oscillator core with a temperature-compensated exponential converter driving a triangle-core oscillator; internal shapers derive sawtooth and a variable-width pulse (PWM) from the triangle. Buffered triangle, sawtooth, and pulse outputs, plus soft sync and hard sync inputs. Requires very few external parts (single timing capacitor, a handful of resistors for scale/HF trim, a 2.5V VREF). Designed for split, regulated +5V/-5V-to--18V supplies rather than the +-12V/+-15V rails typical of vintage synth VCO chips it succeeds in function (e.g. CEM3340-class designs), trading legacy pin compatibility for improved temperature stability and lower component count. Sound Semiconductor's SSI2130 is the higher-feature sibling in the same family, adding an integrated 5-channel mixer, open-collector square output, sine shaper, and through-zero FM/PM.

pins.name: SAW OUT
pins.description: sawtooth generator output, 0V to VREF swing; direction (rising vs falling ramp) set by internal TIME REVERSE state tied to the sync logic. Also fed internally to the (unpopulated on this part) mixer

pins.name: PULSE OUT
pins.description: output of the internal PWM comparator; driven hard to GND or VREF depending on the triangle vs PWM CTRL comparison

pins.name: PWM CTRL
pins.description: second input to the internal PWM comparator, range 0V to VREF; compared against the buffered triangle to produce the variable-width pulse

pins.name: TRI OUT
pins.description: buffered triangle output, swings between GND and VREF at a rate set by TCAP and the exponential converter's output current

pins.name: HF TRACK
pins.description: current output used to trim high-frequency tuning errors caused by bulk emitter resistance in the exponential converter; feed back into EXPO FREQ through a resistor network (fixed or trimmed) for HF compensation, or leave unconnected if not used

pins.name: EXPO FREQ
pins.description: ground-referenced current input to the exponential converter; sensitivity is set by the current into EXPO SCALE, typically 20uA/octave with a 50k ohm resistor for standard 1V/octave response

pins.name: V-
pins.description: negative supply, -4.75V to -18V; recommend a 100nF local decoupling capacitor placed close to the package with short low-inductance traces, plus a dedicated regulator for best noise performance

pins.name: TCAP
pins.description: oscillator timing capacitor to ground; recommended 3.9nF C0G/NP0 or polystyrene for the audio range, usable range 1nF-10nF

pins.name: GND
pins.description: ground; connect with thick short traces or vias to a ground plane

pins.name: HARD SYNC
pins.description: level-sensitive hard sync; when driven high, an internal switch discharges TCAP to ground, resetting the oscillator to the start of its cycle irrespective of phase. Ground directly if unused

pins.name: SOFT SYNC
pins.description: connects through an internal 5k ohm resistor; an AC-coupled pulse causes the falling triangle to reverse direction toward the upper point. Only affects the falling half of the cycle (while TCAP is discharging). Leave unconnected if not used

pins.name: LIN FREQ
pins.description: ground-referenced linear frequency control current input; oscillator frequency is a linear function of this current and stops entirely at zero. Tie to a constant ~5uA (e.g. VREF through 499k ohm) for normal operation if linear FM is not used

pins.name: EXPO SCALE
pins.description: ground-referenced current input that sets the sensitivity (scale) of the EXPO FREQ input; a 20uA/octave scale requires 94.34uA into this pin

pins.name: VREF
pins.description: reference voltage input, must be a stable, low-noise, low-impedance 2.5V (within +-0.5%/+-12.5mV for rated tuning stability); sets waveform amplitude and the EXPO SCALE/LIN FREQ current references

pins.name: BW COMP
pins.description: frequency compensation node for the exponential converter; connect a 270 ohm resistor in series with a 10nF capacitor to ground

pins.name: V+
pins.description: positive supply, regulated +4.75V to +5.25V (typ +5.0V); recommend a 100nF local decoupling capacitor placed close to the package with short low-inductance traces

SOP-16.notes: Per Sound Semiconductor SSI2131 datasheet Rev 2.0, January 2021, page 1 pin-connection diagram ("PIN CONNECTIONS", 16-Lead SOP, top view, JEDEC MS-012-AC) cross-checked against the page 3 pin-description table. Package labeled PSL16 by SSI.

extra.VREF spec: 2.5V +-0.5% (+-12.5mV) required; 100uA max current draw from VREF pin
extra.exponential conformity: 0.3% typ (calibrated per datasheet Expo Setup procedure)
extra.control constant - expo (Iscale): 20uA/octave typ default (94.34uA into EXPO SCALE pin)
extra.sawtooth output drive: 0V-VREF swing, 6mA sink or source typ, discharge time 1.6us typ
extra.pulse/PWM output: 0V-VREF swing, 6mA source typ, rise 70ns/fall 125ns typ, PWM bias current 40nA typ
extra.recommended TCAP: 3.9nF C0G/NP0 or polystyrene for audio range; usable 1nF-10nF

typical_application: Complete VCO front end for an analog synth voice: buffered triangle, sawtooth, and PWM pulse outputs, with 1V/octave exponential control (summed at EXPO FREQ), linear FM (LIN FREQ), and soft/hard sync inputs for classic analog-synth oscillator sync effects.
gotchas: requires two regulated supplies (+5V and -5V to -18V) plus a stable low-noise 2.5V VREF; not a single-rail part and VREF quality directly sets tuning stability

LIN FREQ needs a constant bias current (recommended ~5uA via a 499k ohm resistor from VREF) even when linear FM isn't used, since the oscillator frequency is a linear function of this current and stops entirely at zero

requires a tuning procedure (EXPO SCALE trim, then optional HF TRACK trim) to hit accurate 1V/octave tracking across the ten-octave range; not a plug-and-play fixed-scale part for tonal use, though fixed resistor values are given for LFO-grade applications
HARD SYNC is level-sensitive: holding it high stops the oscillator at GND rather than just resetting phase once; needs a short pulse (capacitively coupled) for edge-triggered sync behavior
TCAP must be a low-tempco C0G/NP0 or polystyrene capacitor; ordinary ceramics will drift tuning with temperature
sold only directly by Sound Semiconductor and its authorized resellers, not a general second-sourced part
successor-in-function to classic CEM3340-family analog synth VCO chips but not pin-compatible; expects modern regulated low-voltage split supplies rather than vintage +-12V/+-15V rails
